judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Skills Objectives in the Geometry topic area, so the same-grain constraint is satisfied. The second SFI (P1, rank 0, Unit 11 'Right angle, Square, and Rectangle', KUC: identify right angle, square and rectangle from other shapes and accurately draw them) asks pupils to '– Draw a square and a rectangle', with LCs 'Draw a square' and 'Draw a rectangle'. The first SFI (P2, rank 1, Unit 11 'Square, rectangle, and triangle', KUC: identify square, rectangle and triangle and calculate perimeter) asks pupils to give examples of materials/objects in and outside the classroom having a similar shape to a square, rectangle and triangle, with LCs for square, rectangle and triangle exemplification. Direction is lower-to-higher rank (P1 -> P2). Hands-on drawing of squares and rectangles at P1 fixes the defining visual properties of those figures, which plausibly supports the later P2 skill of recognising and citing real-world objects with those shapes, now broadened to include the triangle and extended beyond the page to the environment. This is substantive extension (new shape, application to concrete objects), not mere wording repetition, though the shift from production to environmental recognition makes the dependency supportive rather than strict, hence moderate confidence. Note that source and LC evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts shown.
